decision: Official RHOAI 3.5 documentation leaves the backend installation reference unresolved. The installed IPP example identifies OpenMeter as an integration target and Noyitz as the development testing backend. The original pinned Noyitz build and its observed limitations are retained. A local derivative containing the reviewed correctness patch was built and validated locally on 2026-10-19, with patch/image-bound Go and runtime evidence. This does not approve publication, cluster deployment or financial completeness. Keep the deployment selection unset pending integration qualification.

official_documentation_review.scope: RHOAI 3.5 Developer Preview release notes, complete 143-page MaaS book and HTML chapter, installation/component chapter, model-server configuration, and official-linked companion platform/observability pages.
findings: Release notes section 4.1 describes an IPP plugin and PostgreSQL-backed service, plus a separate BBR integration entry. Neither entry supplies a backend image, Operator, chart, manifest or installation link.
MaaS sections 1.8 and 1.18 document observability, usage views and CSV export; they do not install an external metering service. Section 1.5 configures the API-key database, a separate concern.
No external metering backend installation reference was found in the reviewed installation/model-serving chapters or companion platform/observability pages.
This is a documentation gap in the reviewed sources, not proof that no backend artifact exists. Developer Preview status does not establish a supported production backend.
official_documentation_review.actionable_documented_path: For showback, configure dashboard observability, Kuadrant monitoring and tenant telemetry, then view/filter Usage and export CSV. Verify fields against the installed schema. Backend selection remains unresolved.

support_boundary: RHOAI 3.5 external metering is Developer Preview. The linked development service is community source, not a verified Red Hat product backend.

ipp.source_binding: Installed related image and registry config labels git.commit / org.opencontainers.image.revision; checked read-only by parent inventory.

usage.body: one CloudEvents 1.0 object, type inference.tokens.used or inference.request.error

wire_contract.authentication: The shipped IPP client adds no Authorization header and exposes no backend auth-header parameter.
wire_contract.failure_semantics: failOpen allows balance-check errors; hasAccess=false still denies requests. Event delivery errors are logged without a durable queue or retry.
wire_contract.identity: source plus generated event UUID; not a gateway request ID or proof of final client stream completion

profile_customization.preserve: All other existing metadata and data, especially custom-pre-processing-ipp-config.yaml.
profile_customization.lifecycle: After bootstrap/migration MaaS stamps opendatahub.io/managed=false and skips later reconciliation of this ConfigMap. Customize the existing object under that annotation; do not put false in the upstream bootstrap input, which PostRender would drop.
profile_customization.reload: The shipped guide prescribes restarting deployment/payload-processing after changing the profile. No reload or restart has been performed for this demo.
profile_customization.reset: Remove the opt-out annotation for a one-shot reset to defaults, or set opendatahub.io/managed=true for continuous controller management; reload IPP after the intended profile is restored.
profile_customization.configuration_schema: PayloadProcessorConfig llm-d.ai/v1alpha1 is a file-loaded framework schema, not an installed Kubernetes CRD. Plugin configuration uses parameters, not the stale example's json key.
constraints: This is incomplete review data, not an applyable patch; metering.invalid is a reserved placeholder and selected_service_url stays null until the backend is qualified.
Preserve the current single default profile. There is no automatic stream/full-body profile picker.
The framework rejects mixing buffered response processors such as api-translation with response chunk processors in one profile.
The streaming candidate preserves the current OpenAI-compatible response path; other provider response translation needs separate qualification.
The chunk plugin parses both SSE and reassembled nonstreaming JSON usage; both paths still require runtime qualification.
No disabled plugin flag exists. Omitting the plugin from the active profile is the inert state.

reference.source_role: Reference candidate identified by the exact shipped and current upstream IPP examples for testing without OpenMeter. It is not the selected approved backend; this historical source remains unchanged at f9a56b while PriceTag continues its history.
reference.api_compatibility: The unpatched source has matching GET and POST paths; neither handler is behind dashboard authentication. The local derivative preserves these paths and adds strict event validation and replay conflict responses. Its compatibility with actual installed IPP delivery remains unqualified.
reference.registry_metadata_result: Advertised latest reference checked anonymously on 2026-10-18: unauthorized; credentials or public access unavailable, not evidence that the image does not exist. No source-bound backend digest was verified.

build.scope: Historical unpatched source build, 2026-10-18; retained unchanged. See local_correction for the newer derivative.
build.proposed_toolchain: Executed with GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.0; retained binary build information confirms Go 1.26.0.
build.base_metadata_limit: The derived Containerfile pins the verified platform digests. Layers were downloaded and built locally on 2026-10-18; upstream source was unchanged. This is a community backend build, not a Red Hat product operand.
build.toolchain: GOTOOLCHAIN=auto may download Go 1.26 despite the Go 1.25 builder tag; module and toolchain access are prerequisites.
build.target: CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64; binary ./cmd; runtime UID 1001
build.artifact_prerequisite: Local build evidence establishes this candidate artifact only. Publication and OpenShift/IPP integration remain separate, unauthorized steps; neither is implied by local runtime checks.

local_correction.target: Linux amd64; Go 1.26.0; pinned builder/runtime bases retained from the original build route.

validation.postgresql: PostgreSQL 15+ required by NULLS NOT DISTINCT; local Go and runtime validation passed on PostgreSQL 16. PostgreSQL 15 was not separately tested.

implemented_changes: Unique source/event_id and transactional insert/rollup handling: identical JSONB payload replay is a no-op; changed payload or unverifiable legacy history is a conflict. JSONB comparison preserves semantic content and unknown fields, not original whitespace or key order.

Require CloudEvents 1.0, a supported event type, explicit valid timestamp and identity, and six explicit non-null nonnegative int32 counters for usage. Reject total below prompt plus completion, trailing JSON, recursive duplicate keys and case aliases of known fields; do not manufacture totals or timestamps.

Retain token-less native error events with raw_event, usage_complete=false and NULL raw cost. Explicit zero usage remains complete; migrated legacy rows keep NULL completeness and raw payload rather than invented evidence.

Both health endpoints check the primary database with a one-second deadline; event insertion has a two-second deadline. Local probes observed health/readiness 503 during database outage and 200 after recovery, with failed ingestion returning 500 within the bound.
Migration refuses existing duplicate source/event_id history without deleting rows. Reconcile that history explicitly before migration; never rewrite the retained original probe evidence.

runtime.scope: Historical unpatched runtime, validated locally on 2026-10-18; local_correction describes the separately validated newer derivative.
runtime.database: PostgreSQL 14+ per README; startup connects and migrates schema. The example references rhel9/postgresql-16:latest on port 5432, with no verified digest or persistent volume; do not apply that example as a durable ledger.
runtime.probe_limit: Observed locally: both handlers remain 200 during database outage while entitlement returns 500. They do not demonstrate ongoing database or ledger health.
runtime.local_validation: evidence/noyitz-local-20261018/summary.json; local API, database integration, restart and outage checks only. IPP/gateway integration remains unqualified.
runtime.quota: Actual config uses MONTHLY_TOKEN_QUOTA, default 100000000; the example sets 10000000000. Zero falls back to the default, despite stale README text about TOKEN_QUOTA=0. Dollar quota decisions also affect hasAccess. Review and test these before activation.
runtime.optional_integrations: Kubernetes catalog and key-service integrations remain off without their explicit environment configuration. They are not required for the metering wire contract.

historical_unpatched_accounting_limits: The ingestion handler accepts missing numeric fields as zero and invalid timestamps as the current time; it does not qualify billing categories or stream completion.

At this source pin the usage_events table has no event-id uniqueness constraint and InsertEvent has no deduplication. Local replay testing observed two stored rows and doubled entitlement usage for an identical event.

A denied entitlement GET asynchronously inserts a zero-token metering-quota audit row with stored status 429 and increments hourly request totals. Local testing observed this despite the entitlement HTTP response being 200; ledger row counts are not inference request counts.
The database flattens events and does not retain the full original CloudEvent or duration_ms; a lossless export/capture path for this demo has not been verified.
Startup fetches mutable community LiteLLM prices and seeds hosted-model rates separately. Those dashboard costs are not our sourced provider rates, GPU cost allocation or prospective private tariffs.

The backend subtracts cached input from prompt tokens without selecting provider semantics; raw Anthropic uncached-input counts need separate normalization. Unknown model prices fall back to generic rates, so backend monetary totals are not fail-closed financial evidence.
Use retained source events and the existing fail-closed importer/report contracts for financial statements; backend aggregates do not replace their completeness and reconciliation evidence.
accounting_limits: The local derivative's replay, raw-event, strict-usage and health corrections passed Go tests and patch/image-bound local probes. The original unpatched findings are retained separately as history; local validation does not qualify financial completeness or actual gateway integration.

Raw JSONB records preserve semantic event content, including extensions. A qualified capture/export path to the existing importer is still absent; byte-for-byte original wire formatting is not retained.

Incomplete error rows retain NULL raw cost and usage_complete=false. Legacy rows retain unknown completeness. Numeric hourly aggregates use zero arithmetic sentinels and include audit requests, so they cannot establish billing completeness or inference request counts.
Denied entitlement GETs still create zero-token metering-quota audit rows with stored status 429. This is not evidence that a gateway emitted HTTP 429.

Mutable community pricing, separately seeded hosted-model rates, generic unknown-price fallbacks and provider-independent cache subtraction remain unchanged. Backend monetary totals are not the authority for sourced provider rates, GPU allocation or private tariffs.

Actual IPP delivery, stream completion, outage/loss handling, identity mapping, export, provider invoice reconciliation and financial completeness remain unqualified. Use the existing fail-closed importer/report contracts for financial statements.

alternative.qualification_limits: Its event-id-only dedup migration must be applied explicitly and does not perform source+id payload-conflict checking. Missing numeric fields still become zero and missing event times become now. The user usage API aggregates month-to-date linked identities, not lossless original CloudEvents. Actual QUOTA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED defaults true despite README text saying false; model policy can deny access even with quota gating disabled. Shared cache-subtraction and generic unknown-price fallbacks are not our accounting policy. Internal dogfood images are documented as unsuitable for fresh deployment inputs; backend artifact, export, quota policy and end-to-end IPP delivery remain unqualified.

remaining_gates: Choose an approved backend path using the now-established upstream reference chain. Noyitz is the linked testing candidate; PriceTag is its independently verified successor; OpenMeter is the named integration target. No choice is approved by the documentation alone.

The original Noyitz build and the locally validated corrective derivative are retained as separate artifacts. Preserve the exact source/patch/image and probe bindings for any later review or publication; no published image or cluster deployment is selected.

Local PostgreSQL 16 validation passed for corrected replay/concurrency/conflicts, strict usage, NULL-cost error retention, migration refusal, restart persistence and bounded database outage/recovery. Actual IPP/gateway delivery and pricing policy still require separate qualification; gateway activation stays omitted.
Qualify event capture/export, streaming completion, backend outage/loss, identity mapping and provider reconciliation before claiming native financial completeness.
Review the persistent existing-ConfigMap patch and explicit reload/rollback separately; confirm the installed annotation and preservation behavior before activation.
